import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/home/oishi/.openclaw/workspace/data/housing_dataset.csv')

print("Dataset shape:", df.shape)
print("\nColumns:", df.columns.tolist())
print("\nData types:")
print(df.dtypes)

# Separate numerical and categorical columns
numerical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns.tolist()

print("\n\nNumerical columns:", numerical_cols)
print("Categorical columns:", categorical_cols)

# Calculate correlation matrix
correlation_matrix = df[numerical_cols].corr()

# Get correlations with price
price_correlations = correlation_matrix['price'].drop('price').sort_values(ascending=False)

print("\n\n" + "="*60)
print("CORRELATIONS WITH HOUSE PRICE (RANKED)")
print("="*60)

for i, (feature, corr) in enumerate(price_correlations.items(), 1):
    print(f"{i:2}. {feature:20s}: {corr: .4f}")

print("\n" + "="*60)
print("FEATURE ANALYSIS")
print("="*60)

# Interpret correlations
print("\n**Strongest Positive Correlations:**")
for feature, corr in price_correlations.items():
    if corr > 0.5:
        print(f"  {feature}: {corr:.4f} (Strong positive)")

print("\n**Moderate Positive Correlations:**")
for feature, corr in price_correlations.items():
    if 0.3 <= corr <= 0.5:
        print(f"  {feature}: {corr:.4f} (Moderate positive)")

print("\n**Weak Positive Correlations:**")
for feature, corr in price_correlations.items():
    if 0 < corr < 0.3:
        print(f"  {feature}: {corr:.4f} (Weak positive)")

print("\n**No/Negative Correlations:**")
for feature, corr in price_correlations.items():
    if corr <= 0:
        print(f"  {feature}: {corr:.4f} (None/negative)")

# Save results to file
results = price_correlations.to_frame(name='correlation')
results.to_csv('/home/oishi/.openclaw/workspace/feature_correlations_ranked.csv')
print("\n\nResults saved to: feature_correlations_ranked.csv")

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/home/oishi/.openclaw/workspace/data/housing_dataset.csv')

# Create encoded version of categorical variables
df_encoded = df.copy()

# Encode binary/multi-class categorical variables as numeric
# 'yes'/'no' → 1/0
binary_cols = ['mainroad', 'guestroom', 'basement', 'hotwaterheating', 'airconditioning', 'prefarea']
for col in binary_cols:
    df_encoded[col] = df_encoded[col].map({'yes': 1, 'no': 0})

# 'furnishingstatus' → ordinal based on typical value hierarchy
furnishing_order = {'furnished': 3, 'semi-furnished': 2, 'unfurnished': 1}
df_encoded['furnishingstatus'] = df_encoded['furnishingstatus'].map(furnishing_order)

print("Encoded columns:", df_encoded.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist())

# Calculate correlation matrix for encoded data
correlation_matrix = df_encoded.corr()

# Get correlations with price (excluding the price column itself)
price_correlations = correlation_matrix['price'].drop('price').sort_values(ascending=False)

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("ALL FEATURES CORRELATIONS WITH HOUSE PRICE (RANKED)")
print("="*70)

for i, (feature, corr) in enumerate(price_correlations.items(), 1):
    print(f"{i:2}. {feature:20s}: {corr: .4f}")

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("NUMERICAL FEATURES ONLY (Original)")
print("="*70)

numerical_correlations = price_correlations[['area', 'bedrooms', 'bathrooms', 'stories', 'parking']]
for i, (feature, corr) in enumerate(numerical_correlations.items(), 1):
    print(f"{i:2}. {feature:20s}: {corr: .4f}")

print("\n" + "="*70)
print("CATEGORICAL FEATURES (Encoded)")
print("="*70)

categorical_correlations = price_correlations.drop(['area', 'bedrooms', 'bathrooms', 'stories', 'parking'])
for i, (feature, corr) in enumerate(categorical_correlations.items(), 1):
    print(f"{i:2}. {feature:20s}: {corr: .4f}")

# Additional insights
print("\n" + "="*70)
print("KEY INSIGHTS")
print("="*70)

print("\n**Top 3 Most Correlated Features:**")
for i, (feature, corr) in enumerate(price_correlations.head(3).items(), 1):
    print(f"  {i}. {feature}: {corr:.4f}")

print("\n**Feature Impact Classification:**")
for feature, corr in price_correlations.items():
    if abs(corr) >= 0.5:
        impact = "Very High"
    elif abs(corr) >= 0.3:
        impact = "High"
    elif abs(corr) >= 0.1:
        impact = "Moderate"
    else:
        impact = "Low"
    direction = "↑" if corr > 0 else "↓"
    print(f"  {feature:20s}: {corr: .3f} ({impact} impact {direction})")

# Save results
results = price_correlations.to_frame(name='correlation')
results.to_csv('/home/oishi/.openclaw/workspace/feature_correlations_complete.csv')
print("\n\nResults saved to: feature_correlations_complete.csv")
